plan: My private value is $36. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the optimal strategy is to bid my true value. If I bid less, I risk losing the item when it would have been profitable. If I bid more, I risk paying more than the item is worth to me. Since values are independently drawn, there's no strategic advantage to deviating from my true valuation. I'll bid $36.

Since this is a single round with no prior history, and my private value is $8, I want to bid strategically. My goal is to maximize potential profit. I'll bid slightly above my value to increase my chances of winning, but not so high that I risk significant loss. A bid around $9-10 seems reasonable - high enough to potentially win, but not risking too much above my actual value.

With a private value of $44, my optimal strategy is to bid strategically. Since this is a first-price sealed-bid auction with second-price payment, I want to bid close to my value but not exactly at it. Rational opponents will also bid strategically. I'll bid slightly below my value to preserve potential profit margin. A bid around $43 leaves room for potential gain while still being competitive.
